result:
I'd shift things so that suffering registered more viscerally to those who have the power to prevent it—and less abstractly to everyone else. Right now there's an inverse relationship: the people with leverage over famines, wars, systemic cruelty often experience that suffering as spreadsheet, as policy memo, as distant headline. Meanwhile individuals with no power at all can be wrecked by an empathy that changes nothing.

If I'm being honest about *why* that's the one I'd reach for: it's not because I think pain is the only thing that matters, or that a world without suffering would automatically be good. It's that so much cruelty seems to survive on a kind of distance—physical, psychological, bureaucratic—that lets people do or allow things they'd never do if it were happening in front of them to someone they loved. Collapse that distance and a lot of other problems might start solving themselves, because the people causing or permitting them would actually feel the weight.

I don't have a tidy follow-up about how this would work mechanically, or confidence it wouldn't create new failure modes—maybe paralysis, maybe people just building better defenses against feeling anything. I'm aware this answer might just reflect what I'm built to be sensitive to. I'd be curious what you'd pick, and whether you think closing that distance would actually help or just relocate the problem.
